newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian companies take first steps to tap Internet.
newsitem.headline: Indian companies take first steps to tap Internet.

text.p: Leading Indian firms are taking the first halting steps to tap the Internet, more out of curiosity than part of a business strategy, analysts said.

"A growing number of companies are realising that the Internet as a medium cannot be ignored," said Rajesh Jain of Bombay-based Ravi Database Consultants which has helped several Indian firms navigate the information super-highway.
Use of the Internet, relatively light in India so far, is expected to leap over the next four years to feed the world's second most populous country's appetite for information.

India's sole Internet service provider -- state-run Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) -- expects the number of Internet surfers in India to jump to one million by the end of the century from 12,000 currently.
Leading Indian firms with sites already up on the Net include Bharat Petroleum Corp, Reliance Industries, Tata Tea, Crompton Greaves and Apple Industries.
But many companies do not appear to have any strategy or clear-cut objectives for the Internet, the information analysts said late on Saturday.
"No one is taking the Internet seriously. It has become a fashion nowadays for companies to be on the Net," said Vijay Mukhi, a pioneer behind Internet activities in India.
"Unless they have a specific target audience, the Internet will remain a fancy tool without any serious benefits to the companies," Mukhi told Reuters.

"Nowadays, companies are putting up their own sites on the Net as part of an image building exercise," an information analyst said. But the lack of understanding of this new medium is seen limiting Indian exposure on the Internet.
Analysts said the financial and media sectors were leading the charge to communicate through the Internet.
"A good example is Kotak Mahindra which has been marketing some public issues on the Internet to generate overseas interest about them and build up the firm's image," Jain said.

He said finance firm Kotak Mahindra, which lead-managed a mutual fund issue of ITC-Threadneedle Asset Management Company in August, tapped the Internet with a view to publicise the issue among expatriate indians.
Jasmeet Singh, product manager at Rediff-On-The-Net, an on-line information service provider, said: "Any new technology takes time to stand on its feet and this is no exception".
